parts:
Dear Nikola,

Thanks for your script/data. In principle, it should work. But it is
important that when we estimate the CFA models in the first step, we
keep the bifactor pieces together. This means that we must fit the
general factor and its specific factors in one go (and not first the
general factor alone, and then the first specific factor alone, etc). To
accomplish this, you need to use the mm.list= argument as follows:

mm.list = list(bis = "bis", bas = "bas", fight = "fight", freeze =
"freeze", flight = "flight", socanx = c("SOCANX", "SA1", "SA3", "SA4"),
rum = c("RUM" ,"RT", "CFT", "PFT"))

The mm.list defines the 'blocks' that are fitted together. For the
bis/bas/... factors, it is one factor per block. But for socanx and rum,
we fit several factor together:

# sam - local
fit.sam <- lavaan:::sam(proba, data = rsq_rtsq_sas1, sam.method =
"local", estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", verbose = TRUE,
mm.list = mm.list)

Unfortunately, this will not work for your data. The reason is that the
measurement models fit (very) poorly, leading to more 'error' than
'signal' for some of the variables, and this gives computational trouble
later when computing the (two-step) standard errors. At least, when
sam.method = "local".

The only way out (here) is to switch to sam.method = "global":

fit.sam.global <- lavaan:::sam(proba, data = rsq_rtsq_sas1,
sam.method = "global",
estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml",
mm.list = mm.list)

which does work for your model/data combination. The difference between
local/global is somewhat technical. Local sam will explicitly compute an
estimate of the variance/covariance matrix of the latent variables, and
compute the regressions among them in a second step. Global sam does not
explicitly compute this variance matrix, and this can an advantage in
more demanding settings.

Yves.

parts:
Dear Yves, 

 

Thank you a thousand times for your time and effort, and also your kind approach. I am eager to learn about SAM and I am therefore very appreciative of your effort to help. I have one question that is about a problem that, given all this new information, left me confused. 

 

Namely, the global SAM that you have found to be the only to work for my model with bifactors seem to produce a bad fit (which is fair), however, I have noticed that the global SAM-obtained chi-square and df correspond to those I get by applying SEM. The output also produces all these parameters from the measurement model. Now, I do understand that this still is SAM (and I am looking forward to the future papers on SAM), but it seems that the model fit is still evaluated against 2509 degrees of freedom. However, the reviewer that suggested FSR+Croon to me made his suggestion based on the assumption that this will allow me to test the fit of the model that takes only structural relations in consideration (and hence simplifies the model, as  I have hypothesised that the bad fit with MLR SEM is due to model complexity and accompanying misspecifications). More importantly, when I apply local SAM to the model where group-specific factors are taken out (so I have ordinary unidimensional factors for both mediator and outcome instead of the bifactors) - the df is 5 and fit is (no surprise) good. This would allow me to test the fit of the simplified version of my model and answer the review. As I have no publication to rely on, I would be greatly thankful if you told me if I am basing anything here on a wrong assumption on how local SAM works. My question would, in short be, can I use the local SAM as I have described (I get the model with 5 df and only the structural paths and covariances estimated), call this FSR + Croon and cite Devlieger & Rosseel, 2017 (and Devlieger, Mayer, & Rosseel, 2016)? And it uses the total sample? Also, I see that standard errors in local SAM differ when I use MLR as opposed to ML (by a small bit) and so I was wondering if this is relevant.

 

I am sorry to have written my previous question on the google.group as well but the question I asked there is somewhat different (I thought other would find more interesting) and is more about the fsr function which produced strange results for my model - when I take out the group-specific factors of course – fsr function estimates regression paths between the latent variables that are contrary to the ones I get with either MLR or WLSMV SEM (and contrary to those I get from SAM either applied to model with bifactors or not).

 

Best wishes,

Nikola

messages.subject: Re: script and data related to the post about bifactors and lavaan::: sam/FSR+Croon
parts:
On 8/31/20 10:53 PM, Nikola Ćirović wrote:
> Namely, the global SAM that you have found to be the only to work for my
> model with bifactors seem to produce a bad fit (which is fair), however,
> I have noticed that the global SAM-obtained chi-square and df correspond
> to those I get by applying SEM.

That is correct. 'global' SAM still estimates the parameters in 2 steps:
first the measurement part, then (keep the measurement part fixed) the
structural part. To evaluate the model, it uses the same chi-square test
statistic (technically, it is just an approximation) as regular sem.

If you get a 'bad' fit, it is very likely that this is due to some of
the measurement models. This is 'global' fit: both the measurement and
structural part of the model are evaluated together (just like in
regular sem).

> However, the reviewer that suggested FSR+Croon to me made his
> suggestion based on the assumption that this will allow me to test the
> fit of the model that takes only structural relations in consideration

If this is what you really want, then you can use fit the CFA part of
the model (all latent variables in the model, but without the
'structural' part). Then you can extract the variance/covariance matrix
of the latent variables, using

COV <- lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")

and then you can fit the structural part only using 'COV' as the input
covariance matrix. The standard errors will be underestimated, but it
will give you a good sense of the fit of the structural part (only). In
other words, you don't need FSR/SAM for this.

> More importantly, when I apply local SAM to the
> model where group-specific factors are taken out (so I have ordinary
> unidimensional factors for both mediator and outcome instead of the
> bifactors) - the df is 5 and fit is (no surprise) good. This would allow
> me to test the fit of the simplified version of my model and answer the
> review. As I have no publication to rely on, I would be greatly thankful
> if you told me if I am basing anything here on a wrong assumption on how
> local SAM works.

Local SAM is really (almost) identical to FSR+Croon, so you can refer to
the papers of Devlieger et.al.

> My question would, in short be, can I use the local SAM
> as I have described (I get the model with 5 df and only the structural
> paths and covariances estimated), call this FSR + Croon and cite
> Devlieger & Rosseel, 2017 (and Devlieger, Mayer, & Rosseel, 2016)?

> Also, I see that standard errors in local SAM
> differ when I use MLR as opposed to ML (by a small bit) and so I was
> wondering if this is relevant.

The MLR part if only used for the 'first step' (the CFA part of the
model). This may indeed lead to small changes, but usually not much.

Yves.
